public_rationale: The research supports substantial limitations and disagreement about the route to AGI. It does not establish categorical impossibility. Even the skeptical paper allows contemporary LLMs to contribute to broader AGI architectures. Conversely, broad benchmark performance and descriptions of incomplete AGI do not demonstrate a qualifying system. The proposed need for nonexistent computing technology is also unsettled.
limitations: The cited research consists of preprints and does not supply a generally accepted AGI test.
Later model achievements do not automatically establish what the June 2024 systems could support.
Failure to achieve AGI by the evaluation date would not prove impossibility.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Artificial general intelligence is totally impossible to build with any of the generative AI OpenAI makes, and it likely requires number-crunching technology that does not yet exist.
conditions: likely (applies to the requirement for new technology)

statement.excerpt: Why else would Sam Altman talk so often about building artificial general intelligence — a thing that is totally and utterly impossible to build with any of the generative artificial intelligence his company makes, and likely requires number-crunching technology that doesn’t even exist yet?

from_speaker: totally and utterly impossible to build
with any of the generative artificial intelligence his company makes
likely requires number-crunching technology that doesn’t even exist yet
our_interpretation: Read this as a technical claim about whether OpenAI's generative AI approach available at publication could provide a basis for AGI.
Use the ordinary meaning of AGI: broad human-level intellectual competence across domains, rather than success on one benchmark.
The claim is stronger than saying that the products available in June 2024 were not themselves AGI.
Likely qualifies the proposed requirement for new computing technology; it is not a conditional antecedent.
This is a claim about technical feasibility, without a forecast deadline.
criteria.support_condition: A sound and applicable technical result establishes that the relevant generative AI approach cannot yield AGI. Supporting the additional computing claim requires evidence that existing computing technology is insufficient, rather than merely expensive or currently underdeveloped.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reproducibly validated AGI built using the relevant approach, or a sound constructive result establishing its feasibility, contradicts the categorical impossibility claim. An AGI built on computing technology already available at publication would also contradict the asserted technological requirement.

evidence.explanation: The paper argues that contemporary interactive LLMs alone are not a practical route to human-capable AGI, but allows them as components of broader architectures. That distinction prevents using this skeptical analysis as proof of Zitron's unqualified impossibility claim.

The authors report broad capabilities and interpret GPT-4 as an incomplete early form of AGI. Their experiments challenge a categorical dismissal, but neither selected tasks nor that interpretation establish complete AGI or prove future feasibility.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An applicable technical impossibility result, a constructive feasibility result, or independent validation of an AGI with a documented architecture and computing basis.
